Plot a gg_boost_vimp_pool object

Source: R/plot.gg_boost_vimp_pool.R
autoplot.gg_boost_vimp_pool.Rd

Pooled variable importance: for each covariate, the spread over runs of its importance minus that run's shadow band, with the share of runs in which it cleared the band.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gg_boost_vimp_pool'
autoplot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gg_boost_vimp_pool'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A gg_boost_vimp_pool object.

...

Passed to geom_point for the run points.

x

A gg_boost_vimp_pool object.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The layout follows plot.gg_boost_vimp: one panel for the main effect and one for the interaction with time, sharing a variable axis, with covariates running top to bottom by the largest median they reach in either panel.

Each run has its own band, so the runs are not drawn on the importance scale against one shaded band. Instead the x axis is the margin over the band: each run's importance minus the band of that run and panel. Zero is then the line every run was judged against, and a run right of it cleared its band. The box spans the 25th to 75th percentile of the margin across runs, the whiskers the 15th to 85th, and each run is a small point. The label at the right of each row, such as 18/50, counts the runs that cleared the band.

A box well right of zero is a covariate that clears the band in nearly every run; one straddling zero is borderline, and its verdict from any single run is not to be trusted. The share is a measure of stability, not a test.

The x axis is labelled with the metric attribute. The caption gives the number of runs and, when every run records one, the median overall time effect. The returned plot carries no theme.

See also

gg_boost_vimp_pool, plot.gg_boost_vimp

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- boostmtree::simLong(n = 25, n.time = 4, model = 1)$data.list
x <- boost_shadow(sim$features, sim$id, k = 2)
fit <- boostmtree::boostmtree(
  x = x, tm = sim$time, id = sim$id, y = sim$y,
  M = 50, cv.flag = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
runs <- lapply(1:3, function(i) boostmtree::vimp.boostmtree(fit))
plot(gg_boost_vimp(runs))

# }
